A cybersecurity vendor swung to a US$24.9 million quarterly net profit even as it posted an operating loss. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. CrowdStrike Holdings (NASDAQ:CRWD) reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $1.58 billion, representing a 28% increase from $1.23 billion in the same quarter of the previous year, as subscription growth and customer demand supported its cybersecurity business.

Subscription revenue increased 29% year over year to $1.50 billion.

Annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $6.26 billion, up 27% from a year earlier.

The company generated a record $419.2 million in net new ARR during the quarter, highlighting continued demand for its cybersecurity platform.

Cash generation also improved, with operating cash flow reaching a record $665.2 million and free cash flow totaling $474.4 million. CrowdStrike ended the quarter with $5.37 billion in cash and cash equivalents.

Following the quarterly performance, management raised its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook, increasing its net new ARR growth guidance to 45% year over year at the midpoint.

The earnings announcement coincided with CrowdStrike's definitive agreement to acquire Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS) in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion.

Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share held.

The proposed acquisition is expected to combine CrowdStrike's endpoint and workload security capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security platform.

(Nasdaq: CRWD), today announced financial results for the third quarter fiscal year 2027, ended October 31, 2026. “Q3 was the best quarter in CrowdStrike’s history,” said George Kurtz, CrowdStrike’s Founder and Chief Executive Officer.
